subject.title: fix: harden aerith native hook relay recovery

question: Should lost-relay PreToolUse be allowed to no-op for loop-detection-only cases once the source corruption and diagnostic/docs defects are fixed?
rationale: That choice trades availability during Gateway recovery against OpenClaw's fail-closed native tool approval boundary, so automation should not silently decide the permanent policy.

options.title: Preserve approval boundary first
options.body: Keep unavailable PreToolUse fail-closed unless the command can prove no global, trusted, or core approval policy can apply, then require tests and live recovery proof for that distinction.

options.title: Accept the loop-only no-op carveout
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept the availability tradeoff if the PR documents the policy and includes convincing live recovery proof.

options.title: Defer to canonical relay recovery work
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers prefer a narrower restart/regeneration fix from the existing native-hook-relay cluster.

recommendation.title: Preserve approval boundary first
recommendation.body: Keep unavailable PreToolUse fail-closed unless the command can prove no global, trusted, or core approval policy can apply, then require tests and live recovery proof for that distinction.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent ownership signal across native relay, runtime hardening, and test routing surfaces touched by this PR.
